Stop logging Chronicle connection string credentials (#3611)

* Add credential redaction to the Chronicle connection string

A connection string carries the OAuth client secret, the API key and the
certificate password. Nothing could render it without them, so every
diagnostic use of one was a credential in clear text.

BuildRedacted() masks the modelled credentials, and falls back to the option
name for the ones the builder does not model - a connection string carries
arbitrary options, and over-redacting a value costs a little diagnostic
detail where under-redacting one puts it in the log forever.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Stop logging the client secret when connecting to Chronicle

Both connection log messages passed the ChronicleConnectionString itself, so
the formatter rendered it through ToString() - client secret, API key and
certificate password included - at Information level, on every connect and
every watchdog reconnect. Pass the redacted rendering instead.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Document redacting a connection string for logs

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Drop the redundant Class flag from the generated client type attributes

TypeAttributes.Class is 0x0, so a Roslynator brought in by the latest
package update flags 'Public | Class' as a flag already contained in
another (RCS1258) and fails the client snippet verification build.

* Redact by masking the values, not by rendering conditionally

BuildRedacted() threaded a redactSecrets flag through the whole of Build(),
so which credentials reached the result depended on a runtime branch - and a
helper that can return either the mask or the real value is one CodeQL flags
as clear-text logging at every call site, correctly in the sense that nothing
about the shape of the code rules the secret out.

Build a copy that holds no credential at all and render that instead. The
guarantee is now structural rather than conditional, and Build() goes back to
being one unconditional renderer.

The mask is REDACTED rather than ***, because a query parameter value goes
through Uri.EscapeDataString and *** came out as %2A%2A%2A there while the
userinfo kept ***. One mask that survives escaping keeps every redacted value
looking the same.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
